mainTopic: Who breaks the bread and who leads ברכת המזון, where ברכת הזימון ends, and why הטוב והמטיב is not from the Torah.
overview: The גמרא opens with a story. רבי אבהו made a feast for the רבנן after רבי זירא recovered from an illness. At the meal רבי אבהו asked his guest רבי זירא to break the bread and then to lead ברכת המזון, and both times רבי זירא declined by quoting a rule. The גמרא explains that רבי אבהו followed רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the host breaks the bread so he gives generous portions, and the guest leads ברכת המזון so he can bless the host. It then gives the words of that blessing, along with רבי's longer version. Next, רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about where ברכת הזימון ends, at נברך or at הזן. The גמרא tries to tie their argument to two ברייתות that count the blessings differently, but it concludes that each אמורא can explain both ברייתות his own way. Finally, רב יוסף and רב each bring a proof that הטוב והמטיב is not from the Torah. רב's proof relies on a ברייתא about which blessings open and close with 'ברוך', and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי זירא's illness and רבי אבהו's promised feast
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא falls ill. רבי אבהו vows to make a feast for the רבנן if he recovers. He recovers, and the feast is held.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא became sick. רבי אבהו went to visit him and promised: 'If the little man with the scorched legs gets better, I will make a celebration for the Sages.' He got better, and רבי אבהו made a meal for all the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a story. Its purpose is to set the scene for a halachic discussion about who breaks the bread and who leads ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that רבי אבהו is the host (בעל הבית) of this meal, and רבי זירא is the guest of honor. Everything that follows depends on this setup: who is the host and who is the guest.

keyTerms.meaning: became weak or sick
took upon himself; made a vow or resolution
the little one with scorched legs, a nickname for רבי זירא
a festive day; a celebration or feast
he recovered or was healed

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the roles straight. רבי אבהו is the host who made the feast, and רבי זירא is the guest. The whole story turns on this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira became ill,
Rabbi Abbahu went in to visit him,
and he resolved (took upon himself):
If the little one with the scorched legs is healed —
phrases.notes: A nickname for רבי זירא. Elsewhere the גמרא explains that his legs were singed when he tested himself in a fiery furnace.

phrases.english: I will make a festive day (a feast) for the Sages.
He was healed, and he made a meal for all the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that illustrates the laws of breaking bread and leading ברכת המזון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: רבי אבהו is the host of the meal, and רבי זירא is his honored guest.

steps.title: רבי זירא declines to break the bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks רבי זירא to break the bread. רבי זירא cites רבי יוחנן's rule that the host breaks the bread, so רבי אבהו does it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it was time to break bread, רבי אבהו said to רבי זירא: 'Please, master, break the bread for us.' רבי זירא answered: 'Don't you hold like רבי יוחנן, who said the host breaks the bread?' So רבי אבהו broke the bread for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו tries to honor his guest by asking him to break the bread. רבי זירא politely refuses by quoting a halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule says the host (בעל הבית) is the one who breaks the bread, even when an important guest is present. רבי אבהו accepts this and breaks the bread himself, which shows he agrees with this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: to break bread; literally, to begin the meal
doesn't the master hold this? (a polite way of reminding someone of a rule)
the host; the owner of the house
breaks the bread (and says המוציא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the first half of the halacha: at a meal, the host is the one who breaks the bread.

phrases.english: When it came time to break bread,
he (Rabbi Abbahu) said to Rabbi Zeira:
Let the master break bread for us.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the master not hold
that teaching of Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said: The host breaks the bread?
So he (Rabbi Abbahu) broke bread for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא לְמִשְׁרֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The feast from step 1 begins, and the question of who breaks the bread comes up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבי יוחנן, the host breaks the bread. רבי אבהו accepts this and breaks it himself.

steps.title: רבי זירא declines to lead ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks רבי זירא to lead ברכת המזון. רבי זירא responds with רב הונא's rule: whoever breaks the bread also leads the blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it was time to bless, רבי אבהו said to him: 'Please, master, lead ברכת המזון for us.' רבי זירא answered: 'Don't you hold like רב הונא from Bavel, who said the one who broke the bread also leads ברכת המזון?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו again tries to honor רבי זירא, this time by asking him to lead ברכת המזון. רבי זירא pushes back, implying that רבי אבהו should lead it himself, since he broke the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's point is about consistency. רבי אבהו already broke the bread, and according to רב הונא, the same person should lead ברכת המזון. So asking the guest to lead looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: to recite the blessing (ברכת המזון)
רב הונא from Babylonia
the one who broke the bread also leads the after-blessing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules רבי זירא quotes. The first, from רבי יוחנן, is about who breaks the bread. This one, from רב הונא, links the two jobs: whoever breaks the bread also leads ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: When it came time to recite the blessing (Grace after Meals),
he said to him: Let the master bless for us.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the master not hold
that teaching of Rav Huna of Babylonia,
who said: The one who breaks bread recites the blessing?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא לְבָרוֹכֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ נְבָרֵיךְ לַן מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the meal. Since רבי אבהו broke the bread in step 2, רב הונא's rule would require him to lead ברכת המזון too.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's request that the guest, רבי זירא, lead ברכת המזון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב הונא, whoever breaks the bread leads ברכת המזון. רבי אבהו broke the bread, so he should lead it.

steps.title: What was רבי אבהו's own view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion רבי אבהו was following when he asked the guest to lead ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו himself, whose opinion did he follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story to ask a question. It is setting up the next step, which will explain the source behind רבי אבהו's request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו broke the bread but still wanted the guest to lead ברכת המזון. So he clearly did not follow רב הונא. The גמרא wants to know which opinion supports separating the two jobs.

keyTerms.meaning: and he himself (here, רבי אבהו)
in accordance with whom does he hold?

phrases.english: And he (Rabbi Abbahu), in accordance with whom does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 3. If רבי אבהו did not follow רב הונא, what was his source?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי אבהו's view that the host breaks the bread but the guest leads ברכת המזון.

steps.title: The host breaks the bread and the guest leads the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו follows רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the host breaks the bread so he will give generous portions, and the guest leads ברכת המזון so he can bless the host.
steps.simpleTranslation: He followed what רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: The host breaks the bread, and the guest leads ברכת המזון. The host breaks the bread so that he will cut generous pieces. The guest leads ברכת המזון so that he will bless the host.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אבהו followed a fuller version of רבי יוחנן's teaching. That version gives the host the job of breaking the bread and the guest the job of leading ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא had quoted only the first half of רבי יוחנן's rule: the host breaks the bread. The full statement, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, adds that the guest leads ברכת המזון, and it gives a reason for each half. The host cuts generously because it is his own food, while a guest might feel shy to take a big piece. The guest leads ברכת המזון so he can include a blessing for the host.

keyTerms.meaning: a guest
leads the blessing (here, ברכת המזון)
generously; literally, 'with a good eye'
in the name of

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, the host (בעל הבית) breaks the bread, so that he gives generous portions. The guest (אורח) leads ברכת המזון, so that he can bless the host. This disagrees with רב הונא, who holds that whoever breaks the bread also leads ברכת המזון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching explains why רבי אבהו broke the bread himself but still asked his guest to lead ברכת המזון. It also introduces the guest's blessing for the host, which the גמרא goes on to discuss.

phrases.english: In accordance with that which Rabbi Yoḥanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
The host breaks bread, and the guest recites Grace after Meals.
The host breaks bread —
so that he will break it generously (with a good eye).
phrases.notes: A guest might be embarrassed to cut large pieces from someone else's bread.

phrases.english: And the guest recites Grace after Meals —
so that he will bless the host.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by identifying רבי אבהו's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבהו follows רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the host breaks the bread, and the guest leads ברכת המזון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each half of the rule has its own reason: the host gives generous portions, and the guest blesses the host.

steps.title: What does the guest say when he blesses the host?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact words of the guest's blessing for the host.
steps.whatsHappening: In Step 5 we learned that the guest leads ברכת המזון so he can bless the host. Now the גמרא asks what words he actually uses, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 gave the reason for the guest leading but did not give the text of his blessing. This question asks for that missing practical detail.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he bless? What words does he say?

phrases.english: What does he bless (with)?
phrases.notes: "He" means the guest who leads ברכת המזון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the text of the blessing that Step 5 said the guest gives the host.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of the guest's blessing for the host.

steps.title: The basic blessing for the host
steps.stepSummary: The guest asks that the host not be shamed in this world or in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: "May it be Your will that the host not be shamed in this world, and not be embarrassed in the World to Come."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the basic wording: the guest prays that the host never be shamed, in this world or in the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the short core version of the blessing. It covers both worlds: honor in this life and no embarrassment in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: May it be Your will (an opening for a prayer)
The host, the master of the house
Be shamed
Be embarrassed or humiliated
The World to Come

phrases.english: "May it be Your will that the host not be shamed
in this world,
and not be humiliated in the World to Come."

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁלֹּא יֵבוֹשׁ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The guest says: May the host not be shamed in this world or humiliated in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי adds blessings for the host's success
steps.stepSummary: רבי adds requests for success with possessions, protection from the שטן, and protection from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי added more to it: "May he be very successful with all his property. May his property and ours be successful and close to the city. May the שטן have no power over his work or ours. And may no thought of sin, wrongdoing, or iniquity come before him or before us, from now and forever."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) makes the blessing longer by adding requests for the host's money, his work, and his spiritual safety.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic blessing was only about not being shamed. רבי adds practical blessings: success with property, fields close to the city, and protection from the שטן and from sin. He also includes the guests ("and ours"), so the blessing is shared.

keyTerms.meaning: His possessions or property
The Satan, the force that causes harm and failure
A thought of sin
Iniquity, wrongdoing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי is replacing the basic blessing. He keeps it and adds more to it ("מוסיף בה").

phrases.english: And Rebbi adds things to it:
"And may he be very successful with all his possessions,
and may his possessions and our possessions be successful
and close to the city,
phrases.notes: Fields close to town are easy to watch over and care for.

phrases.english: and may the Satan not have control

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂי יָדָיו וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂי יָדֵינוּ,
phrases.english: not over his handiwork and not over our handiwork,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יִזְדַּקֵּר לֹא לְפָנָיו וְלֹא לְפָנֵינוּ
phrases.english: and may there not come up, not before him and not before us,
any thought of sin,
transgression, or iniquity
from now and forever."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the basic blessing text given in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי adds blessings for material success, protection from the שטן, and protection from sin, for both the host and the guests.
steps.whatToRemember: The guest's blessing for the host has a short core (no shame in either world) and a longer version from רבי (success, protection from the שטן, freedom from sin).

steps.title: Where does ברכת הזימון end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: how far does ברכת הזימון go?
steps.simpleTranslation: Until where does ברכת הזימון go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It asks where the special group part of the blessing, the זימון, ends. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When three people eat together, there is a special opening called the זימון before ברכת המזון. The question is about the boundary: does the זימון include only the opening invitation, or also part of the regular blessings?

keyTerms.meaning: Until where? How far does it go?
The blessing of the group invitation, said when three or more ate together

phrases.english: Until where is the zimmun blessing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the guest's blessing for the host to a new question about the limits of the זימון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact ending point of ברכת הזימון.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the זימון ends at "נברך". רב ששת says it goes until "הזן", the end of the first blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says: until "Let us bless" (נברך). רב ששת says: until "Who feeds" (הזן).
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers. רב נחמן says the זימון is only the invitation. רב ששת says it continues through the first blessing of ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the זימון is just the call "נברך" (Let us bless) and its response. For רב ששת, the זימון also includes the first blessing, which ends "הזן את הכל" (Who feeds all). So the disagreement is about whether the first blessing belongs to the זימון unit or to the regular ברכת המזון. On Rashi's reading, which the next steps follow, this has a practical result: the זימון needs three, so for רב ששת people eating without a זימון do not say הזן at all (Rashi 46a).

keyTerms.meaning: "Let us bless", the invitation line of the זימון
"Who feeds", the closing words of the first blessing of ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: Rashi and Tosafot read this dispute differently. Rashi (followed in steps 11-15): the זימון needs three, and for רב ששת it runs through הזן, so without a זימון הזן is not said. Tosafot rejects that, since הזן is from the Torah and every individual says it. Tosafot reads the dispute as how long one who stops eating for the other two must wait: until 'נברך', or until they finish הזן. On Tosafot's reading, ברכת המזון is said in full either way.
steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing where the זימון ends tells us which part of the blessing belongs to the group unit and which part is the regular ברכת המזון. The גמרא next tests this argument by trying to match it to a dispute between two ברייתות (steps 11-15).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says: until "Let us bless,"
and Rav Sheshet says: until "Who feeds."
phrases.notes: "Who feeds" is the ending of the first blessing: "Blessed are You... Who feeds all."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 with two competing opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: the זימון ends at "נברך". רב ששת: it extends through "הזן", the end of the first blessing.

steps.title: Proposing a parallel dispute between two ברייתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument of רב נחמן and רב ששת matches a dispute of תנאים, and quotes two conflicting ברייתות about the number of blessings in ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute between תנאים. One ברייתא teaches: ברכת המזון is two and three blessings. Another ברייתא teaches: it is three and four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It brings two ברייתות that give different numbers of blessings, and it will try to link them to the argument of רב נחמן and רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On Rashi's reading, each ברייתא gives two numbers: one for when there is no זימון and one for when there is. The ברייתות do not agree on the numbers. That gap is a hint that they may disagree about how much of the text belongs to the זימון. (Tosafot, following the רי״ף, reads the numbers as how many people share the recitation, not as blessings left out.)

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים (a proposed earlier parallel)
Grace after Meals
the other one

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute between Tannaim,
for one baraita teaches:
Grace after Meals is two and three blessings,
and the other baraita taught: three and four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to find an earlier source behind the אמוראים' dispute in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב נחמן and רב ששת about where the זימון ends
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two conflicting ברייתות about the number of blessings in ברכת המזון

steps.title: Matching each ברייתא to one side of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: Assuming everyone agrees that הטוב והמטיב is not from the Torah, the גמרא proposes that 'two and three' means the זימון runs until הזן, and 'three and four' means it ends at נברך.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that everyone agrees הטוב והמטיב is not a Torah-level blessing. So isn't this what they argue about? The one who says 'two and three' holds the זימון goes until הזן. The one who says 'three and four' holds it goes only until נברך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proposal. It links the ברייתא of 'two and three' to רב ששת and the ברייתא of 'three and four' to רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא first removes one possible cause of the different numbers: everyone treats הטוב והמטיב as not from the Torah. With that out of the way, the only remaining explanation seems to be where the זימון ends. If הזן is part of the זימון, then per Rashi people without a זימון do not say it, so the counts are smaller. If the זימון ends at נברך, the זימון adds a whole extra blessing on top of the regular ones.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the students) assumed
'Who is good and does good,' the fourth blessing
required by Torah law
Is it not that...? (introduces a proposed explanation)
they disagree

phrases.english: They assumed
that according to everyone, 'Who is good and does good'
is not from Torah law.
So is it not that they disagree about this:
the one who says two and three
holds that the zimmun extends until 'Who feeds all.'
And the one who says three and four
holds that it extends only until 'Let us bless.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proposal begun in step 11 by assigning each ברייתא to one view.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן and רב ששת each follow a different תנא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The different blessing counts in the two ברייתות, read through the assumption about הטוב והמטיב
steps.confusionAlert: On Rashi's reading, 'Two and three' and 'three and four' are not four separate opinions. Each ברייתא gives one count without a זימון and one count with a זימון.

steps.title: Rejecting the parallel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proposal. Each אמורא can explain both ברייתות according to his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רב נחמן can explain both according to his reasoning, and רב ששת can explain both according to his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proposal. It says neither אמורא is forced into one ברייתא, and it sets up the two explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal assumed the ברייתות could only disagree about where the זימון ends. The rejection says there are other ways to explain the different numbers. Because of that, the ברייתות do not prove which side each אמורא is on.

keyTerms.meaning: No (a rejection of the proposal)
explains (the sources) according to his own reasoning

phrases.english: No;
Rav Nachman explains according to his reasoning,
and Rav Sheshet explains according to his reasoning:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תנאים parallel proposed in steps 11-12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that the dispute between the אמוראים depends on the dispute between the ברייתות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The different blessing counts can be explained in other ways, so each אמורא can fit both ברייתות to his view.

steps.title: רב נחמן's explanation: the workers' blessing
steps.stepSummary: According to רב נחמן, both ברייתות agree the זימון ends at נברך. The 'two and three' ברייתא is talking about the shortened ברכת המזון said by workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן explains: everyone agrees the זימון goes until נברך. The ברייתא that says 'three and four' fits well. The one that says 'two and three' is talking about the workers' blessing. As the Master said: a worker opens with הזן and includes בונה ירושלים inside the blessing of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב נחמן fits the 'two and three' ברייתא into his view. That ברייתא is talking about workers, who say a shorter ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worker says only two blessings: הזן, and the blessing of the land with בונה ירושלים folded into it. Add the זימון, which ends at נברך, and the count becomes three. So the smaller numbers come from the workers' short version, not from הזן being part of the זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: fine, it works well
the shortened ברכת המזון said by workers
we are dealing with
'Who builds Jerusalem,' the third blessing
the blessing of the land, the second blessing

phrases.english: Rav Nachman explains according to his reasoning:
everyone agrees it is until 'Let us bless.'
The one who says three and four — fine.
And the one who says two and three —

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָךְ הָכָא בְּבִרְכַּת פּוֹעֲלִים עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: he would tell you: here we are dealing with the workers' blessing,
as the Master said: he opens with 'Who feeds all'
and includes 'Who builds Jerusalem' in the blessing of the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עַד ״נְבָרֵךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the rejection in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting one ברייתא to a special case (workers)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'two and three' ברייתא seemed to require that הזן is part of the זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is talking about workers' shortened ברכת המזון, so it fits a זימון that ends at נברך.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that workers may shorten ברכת המזון, a practical halachic allowance.

steps.title: רב ששת's explanation: the fourth blessing as Torah law
steps.stepSummary: According to רב ששת, both ברייתות agree the זימון runs until הזן. The 'three and four' ברייתא holds that הטוב והמטיב is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת explains: everyone agrees the זימון goes until הזן. The ברייתא that says 'two and three' fits well. The one that says 'three and four' holds that הטוב והמטיב is a Torah-level blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב ששת fits the 'three and four' ברייתא into his view. It drops the earlier assumption that everyone agrees הטוב והמטיב is not from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal in step 12 rested on the idea that all the תנאים treat הטוב והמטיב as rabbinic. רב ששת rejects that idea. For him, the 'three and four' ברייתא gets its higher count by counting הטוב והמטיב as a Torah blessing, not because the זימון ends earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds
'Who feeds all,' the first blessing of ברכת המזון

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet explains according to his reasoning:
everyone agrees it is until 'Who feeds all.'
The one who says two and three — fine;
and the one who says three and four
holds that 'Who is good and does good' is from Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עַד ״הַזָּן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second half of the rejection in step 13, matching רב נחמן's explanation in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a hidden assumption of the proposal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds הטוב והמטיב is not from the Torah, so 'three and four' must mean the זימון ends at נברך.
steps.terutzMaskana: That תנא holds הטוב והמטיב is from the Torah, which explains his higher count even with a זימון that runs until הזן.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתות do not settle the argument between רב נחמן and רב ששת. רב נחמן explains 'two and three' as the workers' short blessing. רב ששת explains 'three and four' as counting הטוב והמטיב as a Torah blessing.

steps.title: Workers skip it, so it cannot be a Torah blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves that הטוב והמטיב is not from the Torah, because workers are allowed to leave it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: You can see that 'הטוב והמטיב' is not from the Torah, because workers leave it out completely.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a proof that the fourth blessing of ברכת המזון, הטוב והמטיב, is not a Torah requirement. His proof is that workers are allowed to skip it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned in step 14 that workers say a shortened ברכת המזון so they can get back to work quickly. חז״ל could never permit skipping a blessing that the Torah requires. Since workers may drop הטוב והמטיב, it must be a rabbinic blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: You should know / you can see (a formula that opens a proof)
'Who is good and does good', the fourth blessing of ברכת המזון
Not from the Torah (only rabbinic)
Workers hired by an employer
Uproot, meaning leave out completely

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general rule that הטוב והמטיב is rabbinic, while the first three blessings of ברכת המזון are from the Torah.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Know that 'Who is good and does good' is not from the Torah —
phrases.notes: 'תדע' signals that a proof is coming.

phrases.english: for workers leave it out.
phrases.notes: This refers back to the workers' shortened ברכת המזון from step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the steps that used the idea that הטוב והמטיב might not be from the Torah, the גמרא now brings independent proof that it really is not from the Torah.
steps.raayaObject: That הטוב והמטיב is a rabbinic blessing, not a Torah one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The halacha that workers may leave הטוב והמטיב out of their shortened ברכת המזון.

steps.title: The wording of the blessing shows it is not from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, quoting רב, proves that הטוב והמטיב is not from the Torah because it opens with 'ברוך' but does not close with 'ברוך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: You can see that 'הטוב והמטיב' is not from the Torah, because it opens with 'ברוך' but does not close with 'ברוך'.
steps.whatsHappening: A second proof is brought, this time from the blessing's wording. הטוב והמטיב opens with 'ברוך' but has no closing 'ברוך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three Torah blessings of ברכת המזון are a connected series. A blessing attached to the one before it does not open with 'ברוך'. Because הטוב והמטיב does open with 'ברוך', it is treated as a separate blessing that stands alone and was added later, so it is not part of the Torah's ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of רב (quoting him)
Opens with 'Blessed are You'
Closes with 'Blessed are You' (a closing line like 'ברוך אתה ה׳...')

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that the missing closing 'ברוך' alone is the whole proof. The point is that this wording pattern marks it as a separate, stand-alone blessing and not part of the connected Torah series. The ברייתא that follows explains this pattern.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said
in the name of Rav:
Know that 'Who is good and does good' is not from the Torah,
for one opens it with 'Blessed'
but does not close it with 'Blessed',

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב תִּדַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate proof for the same conclusion as רב יוסף in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That הטוב והמטיב is a rabbinic blessing, not a Torah one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the blessing: it opens with 'ברוך' but does not close with it.

steps.title: A ברייתא about which blessings open and close with 'ברוך'
steps.stepSummary: To support רב's proof, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא. Normally every blessing opens and closes with 'ברוך', but there are exceptions, and some of them open with 'ברוך' without closing with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: All blessings open with 'ברוך' and close with 'ברוך', except for blessings over fruit, blessings over מצוות, a blessing that is attached to the blessing before it, and the last blessing after קריאת שמע. Among these, some open with 'ברוך' and do not close with 'ברוך'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains the normal pattern of blessings and lists the exceptions. This is the background for רב's proof, and the ברייתא continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that a blessing both opens and closes with 'ברוך'. The ברייתא now sorts the exceptions. One group, such as fruit and מצוה blessings, are short blessings that open with 'ברוך' but have no closing. הטוב והמטיב follows this pattern, so it is a stand-alone blessing. The other group, which comes next in the ברייתא, closes with 'ברוך' without opening with it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The blessing over fruit, said before eating
The blessing said before doing a מצוה
A blessing attached to the blessing before it, so it does not open with 'ברוך'
The reading of שמע

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא lists four exceptions, but they do not all work the same way. Some of them open with 'ברוך' without closing; these are the fruit and מצוה blessings. Others are the opposite: they close with 'ברוך' without opening; these are the attached blessing and the last blessing after שמע. On this amud the ברייתא only begins the first group, and it does not yet name which blessings belong to it. It finishes the division on the next amud.

phrases.english: As it was taught: All blessings, every one of them,
one opens them with 'Blessed'
and closes them with 'Blessed',
except for the blessing over fruit and the blessing over מצוות,
and a blessing attached to the one before it,
and the last blessing of Shema.
Some of them one opens with 'Blessed'
but does not close with 'Blessed',
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud with the opposite group.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: כׇּל הַבְּרָכוֹת כּוּלָּן פּוֹתֵחַ בָּהֶן בְּ״בָרוּךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that is the source for the blessing-wording pattern used in רב's proof in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The wording rule behind רב's proof: blessings that open with 'ברוך' without closing are stand-alone, short blessings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the exceptions to the rule that blessings open and close with 'ברוך'.
